headline: Indonesia Achieves Universal Health Coverage for 98% in a Decade
meta_description: Indonesia expanded health insurance from 121 million to 280 million members in 10 years, reaching 98% of its 287 million population.
summary_short: Indonesia's national insurance program grew dramatically over a decade, consolidating coverage to reach nearly universal health care for its population.
body:
Indonesia has achieved universal health coverage for 98% of its 287 million people in just 10 years—a remarkable expansion of its national insurance program. The transformation began with 121 million members and grew to 280 million through consolidation of the system.

This achievement demonstrates what rapid institutional reform can accomplish at scale. By streamlining multiple programs into a unified national scheme, Indonesia managed to extend care to hundreds of millions of its citizens in a single decade.

The milestone reflects both political commitment and practical execution. For a nation of nearly 300 million people, reaching near-universal coverage represents one of the most ambitious public health undertakings in recent history.
quick_facts: 98% coverage of Indonesia's 287 million population achieved
Membership grew from 121 million to 280 million
Universal health coverage accomplished in just 10 years
Program consolidated multiple insurance schemes into one system
